chapter: Cab Calloway's band: road, arrangers and shows
title: Mother Haylow's brownstone in Philadelphia
summary: Bandleaders like Duke and Basie stayed at her house, where tunes were written; others ate in the basement and played pinochle with her.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And there were some wonderful places that I‟m really, really trying to recall. Like Philadelphia had a lady named Mother Havlow. This lady had a brownstone there, whatever you call it. It must have been about four stories because on the first floor was like a nice living room for the piano in there, and a sitting room and a bedroom. This was where all the bandleaders… Duke, Basie stayed there. Her kitchen and her dining room where we ate was in a basement and after the meal… she loved to play pinochle so if you played pinochle with her you‟re in good shape. But this room on the first floor was for the bandleaders. Now the band‟s [unintelligible] would go up. I was always up on the top floor [laughter] there some place. But there‟s no telling how many songs and tunes and things that were written in Mother Haylow‟s
house there in Philadelphia. It was a mainstay of the places for the bandleaders to stay. I was talking to Basie about it many times.
